findings.explanation: Equality on v is `fun _ _ => sorry`, one indeterminate Bool independent of its arguments. All definitions using `==` on v (check_type BoolT, the_Boolv, do_if, do_log, compiler_agrees, do_eval; HOL4 lines 194, 185, 704, 739, 535, 549) therefore lose HOL4's real equality. Lean proves do_if a e1 e2 = do_if b e1 e2 for all a, b. HOL4 has do_if (Boolv T) e1 e2 = SOME e1 and do_if (Boolv F) e1 e2 = SOME e2. Lean's do_if can never reach the else branch, since both tests are the same Bool. do_log, check_type BoolT and do_eval are similarly wrong. The sem_env instance on line 32 has the same defect but is unused in this module.
findings.repair:
open Classical in
noncomputable instance : BEq v := ⟨fun a b => decide (a = b)⟩
open Classical in
noncomputable instance : BEq sem_env := ⟨fun a b => decide (a = b)⟩
-- and mark the definitions that use them noncomputable
findings.lean_check:
import LeanTypeSound.SemanticPrimitives

example (a b : v) (e1 e2 : exp) : do_if a e1 e2 = do_if b e1 e2 := rfl
findings.hol4_check: e1 <> e2 ==> do_if (Boolv T) e1 e2 <> do_if (Boolv F) e1 e2

findings.explanation: In the IntT Div and Mod cases, HOL4's `/` and `%` on int are int_div and int_mod (integerScript.sml:1989, 2074). These are floor division and the matching modulus, whose sign follows the divisor. Lean's `/` and `%` on Int are Euclidean (ediv/emod), so the results differ when the divisor is negative and does not divide the dividend. For 7 and -2, HOL4 gives Div = -4 and Mod = -1; Lean gives Div = -3 and Mod = 1. The same error reaches do_app (Arith Div IntT) and (Arith Mod IntT).
findings.lean_check:
import LeanTypeSound.SemanticPrimitives

example : do_arith .Div .IntT [.Litv (.IntLit 7), .Litv (.IntLit (-2))] = some (.inr (.Litv (.IntLit (-3)))) := by
  first | rfl | simp [do_arith, the_Litv_IntLit]

example : do_arith .Mod .IntT [.Litv (.IntLit 7), .Litv (.IntLit (-2))] = some (.inr (.Litv (.IntLit 1))) := by
  first | rfl | simp [do_arith, the_Litv_IntLit]
findings.hol4_check: do_arith Div IntT [Litv (IntLit 7); Litv (IntLit (-2))] = SOME (INR (Litv (IntLit (-4)))) /\ do_arith Mod IntT [Litv (IntLit 7); Litv (IntLit (-2))] = SOME (INR (Litv (IntLit (-1))))

findings.explanation: The only equation HOL4 saves is the_Litv_IntLit (Litv (IntLit i)) = i; the value on every other v is unspecified. Lean uses `default`, so it proves for example the_Litv_IntLit (Loc true 0) = 0.
findings.repair:
opaque the_Litv_IntLit_unspec : v → Int
def the_Litv_IntLit : v → Int
  | .Litv (.IntLit i) => i
  | x => the_Litv_IntLit_unspec x
findings.lean_check:
import LeanTypeSound.SemanticPrimitives

example : the_Litv_IntLit (.Loc true 0) = 0 := by first | rfl | decide
